headline: Sustainability is lasting over time—designing systems that can continue indefinitely
universal_truth: What can't continue, won't; if you're borrowing from the future, the bill eventually comes due
fun_facts: The oldest living tree is over 5,000 years old—some systems can last for millennia
Most businesses fail within 10 years—longevity is the exception, not the rule
Ancient Rome lasted 1,000 years; the average civilization lasts about 340 years
discussion_questions: What in your life is sustainable long-term?
What are you doing now that you couldn't maintain for 10 years?
How do you balance short-term and long-term?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Empires rise and fall. Companies come and go. Even stars eventually burn out. But some things last—trees for millennia, cultures for centuries, habits for lifetimes. What makes some things sustainable while others collapse?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often optimize for short-term gains at long-term cost. But unsustainable practices eventually fail. What makes something able to last?

options.text: Sustainability requires not consuming more than is replenished—living within means, maintaining what you depend on, leaving enough for continuation
options.response: Yes. Sustainability is living within the budget—whether resources, energy, relationships, or health. Taking more than is replenished is borrowing from the future, and debts come due.

options.text: Things that are important to people will last
options.response: Importance helps, but even important things fail if they consume more than they regenerate...

q1.title: Resource Balance
q1.script: Sustainable systems don't consume more than they replenish. Overfishing depletes oceans. Overwork depletes people. The math is simple: take more than regenerates, and eventually there's nothing left.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Resource Balance"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Maintenance Matters
q2.script: Nothing lasts without maintenance. Roads need repair. Relationships need attention. Skills need practice. Sustainability isn't just about not over-consuming—it's about actively maintaining what you depend on.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Sustainability
q3.script: Your lifestyle, pace, habits—are they sustainable? Could you live this way for 20 years? If not, something will break. Building sustainable patterns now prevents future collapse.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What can't continue, won't. If you're borrowing from the future, the bill eventually comes due. Build for sustainability, not just success.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 214. Tomorrow, we'll explore fitting your environment—adaptation. Until then, audit one area of life for sustainability.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Sustainability Audit - Can This Continue?
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate long-term sustainability of current patterns
growTrack.activity: Pick one area—work pace, spending, health habits, relationship investment. Could you sustain this for 20 years? If not, what would sustainable look like? Small adjustments now prevent forced changes later.
